# Log10x POC — local source (file)

_Pulled 12K log lines (2.33 MB) across 30 files (tail-sampled; the `window` parameter does not apply to files)._

## Sample composition

These files produced the bytes in the sample. **Confirm this looks like your production mix before trusting the projection** — if 70% of your real-prod bytes come from a service that is NOT in this list, the savings projection is meaningless to you. Widen `paths` or raise `max_pods` (the file cap) if anything looks off.

| `kafka` | 0.341 MB | 1.9K | 15% |

## Projected savings at industry list pricing

_Rate source: list price (vendors.json). Pass `effective_ingest_per_gb` on `log10x_estimate_savings` or `log10x_savings` once your real $/GB is known to convert these projections into a customer-specific quote._

If your full ingest mix matches this sample, ~67% of your byte volume is non-error high-frequency patterns — candidates for compacting, tiering down or offloading, each of which keeps every line.

**Projected daily ingest** (extrapolated from sample): 5.6 MB.

_File tails carry no time span of their own; the daily projection assumes the sampled bytes cover `10h` (the `window` argument). Pass the window the files actually span to make this projection honest._

_These are list-price figures, not predictions of your specific bill — use them to size the order of magnitude, not to negotiate with procurement._
